issues.evidence: All three calls fail immediately after name confirmation, before any bank operation. The supplied traces do not include the underlying Python exception.
issues.problem: The evaluator defines helpers that depend on script-level state and uses global prefix inside those helpers. That is unsafe when the executor wraps the snippet or executes it with separate global and local namespaces. The exception handler then hides the cause.
issues.fix: Place evaluator state, imports and helpers inside one explicitly invoked function. Use a mutable closure for accumulated speech, remove global declarations, and retain a private diagnostic on failure.

issues.problem: technical_hold has no extraction, tools or transitions. It ignores subsequent human requests, identity refusals and repeated statements that the customer wants to stop. This directly explains the observed error and goodbye loops.
issues.fix: Turn it into a restricted recovery intake. Evaluate fresh recovery replies under the original privacy, human-request and refusal rules. Never turn a calculation failure into authorization or invent a successful bank result.

issues.problem: The initial TTS opening does not initialize workflow state. The evaluator relies on system.conversation being available as an ordinary variable, although caller-first starts and missing transcript variables are possible.
issues.fix: Extract whether the opening and name question actually appeared in recent assistant speech. Reconcile that evidence with existing state and transcript evidence before counting the reply.

issues.problem: A human request received around the final successful security result can enter the help-first conversation while authorization is complete but account data is absent. The current evaluator treats that legitimate intermediate state as a technical failure.
issues.fix: Process help-first replies before requiring loaded account data. Fetch the account only after authorization; permit a general human transfer without an account lookup.

issues.problem: A floor rejected during proposal confirmation can be offered again as attempt 1, despite the floor-once rule. Ambiguous replies to the human question also cause the help-first question to be repeated indefinitely.
issues.fix: Track rejected floor offers independently from persuasion attempts. Only late-band attempt 2 may repeat the floor. Ask the help-first question once and preserve any substantive answer supplied afterward.

issues.problem: The previous checks did not establish that the evaluator could run in the platform execution scope. Several checks also asserted speech without inspecting computed deadlines.
issues.fix: Append startup, recovery, authorization, band-edge, split-answer and write-sequence regression checks. These are authored checks, not executed test results. The source still supplies no alternative successful closing protocol for a failed close_call; do not fabricate one or retry that operation silently.

value.name: technical_hold

on_enter.text: I could not complete that action.

value.task_message: A required operation or policy calculation was unavailable. Wait for the caller's reply; no conversation tool is allowed. The engine evaluates that reply. Do not repeat a goodbye, claim completion, disclose unverified account information or invent a security question. The permitted recovery actions are resuming the original authorized question, answering an AI or scam question, handling a request for a person with the one help-first question, or applying the source's identity-refusal and twice-do-not-talk rules. A failed final bank closure does not authorize a duplicate close or a false successful hangup.

extraction_schema.name: recovery_event
extraction_schema.description: Newest reply only. human requests a person; no_talk explicitly ends or declines the conversation, including an actual goodbye; about asks the purpose; ai asks whether this is an AI; scam questions authenticity; resume asks to continue or retry; unknown is unclear speech, confusion or another question. none means no fresh reply. Do not classify mere confusion as refusal.

transitions.description: Handle the fresh recovery reply under the applicable source rules without granting authorization.

patches.value: The brief specifies the two-attempt failure outcome only for create_promise. Other unsuccessful operations must never be reported as successful or relabeled as failed security answers. Recovery preserves the original authorization boundary and honors subsequent human requests, identity refusals and twice-do-not-talk statements. Explicit resumption may repeat an operation that the contract says was not carried out; it does not reset a create_promise budget. A failed close_call remains an unresolved contract case: exactly one invocation and success-gated hangup cannot both be satisfied after that failure. No duplicate close or invented closing code is used.

Static review only; no tools or checks were executed. The observed calls establish an early evaluator failure and an unrecoverable fallback loop, but do not expose the original exception. The replacement isolates Python helper state in one function closure and records private diagnostics. Added checks cover the startup path, actual opening delivery, recovery, authorization before lookup, numerical calendar facts, split security input, confirmation and actual write results. Hand-supplied extraction values do not demonstrate live extraction or dialogue success. No usable synthetic customer call inputs were supplied; smoke remains omitted. Individual-brief mode omits scenarios.
